provenance.title: Postnatal maternal danger signs
provenance.primarySource: WHO PNC DAK v1.0.0 (PNC danger-sign decision tables); WHO recommendations on postnatal care of the mother and newborn
provenance.why: Most maternal deaths happen after birth, not during it, and the postnatal danger signs are the ones a woman and her family must be told to come back for. Secondary haemorrhage, puerperal sepsis, postpartum pre-eclampsia and venous thromboembolism all present in the days and weeks after discharge, when she is at home and no longer being watched.

sourceVerification.vendoredArtefact: docs/reference/who-dak/dak-pnc-v1.0.0 — PNC danger-sign decision tables inform the sign list
sourceVerification.note: The danger-sign vocabulary is PNC-DAK-derived; the thresholds and the actions are national. A postpartum hypertensive presentation is treated the same as the antenatal one via the shared hypertensive-disorders family. blocksRatification stays true pending ratification of the actions.
sourceVerification.safetyInvariant: A CRITICAL maternal signal here is non-overridable and must never be suppressed by any bereavement or sensitivity filter downstream. A woman after a stillbirth or loss is at HIGHER risk of haemorrhage, sepsis and thromboembolism, not lower — suppressing her danger signs out of a misplaced gentleness would kill her. Thoughts of self-harm are CRITICAL for the same reason.

rules.name: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage
rules.message: Heavy or increasing bleeding after birth — treat as postpartum haemorrhage now.
rules.explanation: Bleeding that is heavy, or increasing rather than settling, in the days after birth is secondary PPH — often retained products or endometritis. It is an emergency wherever it happens, including at home.
rules.requiredAction: Resuscitate, give a uterotonic, and refer urgently. Examine for retained products and infection; secondary PPH is frequently both bleeding and sepsis.

adaptation.whoStatement: Heavy or increasing postnatal bleeding requires urgent assessment for secondary postpartum haemorrhage.

rules.name: Puerperal sepsis
rules.message: Puerperal sepsis — start antibiotics and refer.
rules.explanation: Fever with offensive lochia or lower abdominal pain after birth is puerperal sepsis until proven otherwise, and she compensates until she does not. Do not wait for a culture.
rules.requiredAction: Give broad-spectrum antibiotics empirically, resuscitate, and refer. Assess for retained products needing evacuation.

adaptation.whoStatement: Fever with offensive lochia or uterine tenderness postnatally indicates puerperal sepsis requiring immediate antibiotics.

testCases.name: fever alone with no local sign does not

rules.name: Postpartum eclampsia / severe pre-eclampsia
rules.message: Postpartum eclampsia or severe pre-eclampsia — magnesium sulfate and control the blood pressure.
rules.explanation: Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia do not end at delivery — a substantial share of eclampsia is postpartum, sometimes days after discharge. A convulsion, a severe blood pressure, or headache with visual disturbance after birth is this until proven otherwise.
rules.requiredAction: Give magnesium sulfate, treat severe hypertension, and refer. The same pathway as antenatal severe pre-eclampsia.

adaptation.whoStatement: Hypertension, headache with visual disturbance, or convulsions in the postnatal period require management for pre-eclampsia/eclampsia.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published; managed on the shared hypertensive-disorders pathway.

rules.name: Venous thromboembolism
rules.message: Possible deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism — assess and refer urgently.
rules.explanation: The postpartum period is the highest-risk time in a woman's life for venous thromboembolism. Unilateral calf pain or swelling is a possible DVT; chest pain or breathlessness is a possible pulmonary embolism and can be rapidly fatal.
rules.requiredAction: Assess and refer urgently. Chest pain or breathlessness is a medical emergency — do not attribute breathlessness to normal postpartum recovery without excluding PE.

adaptation.whoStatement: Calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness in the postnatal period requires urgent assessment for venous thromboembolism.

rules.name: Thoughts of self-harm or harming the baby
rules.message: Thoughts of self-harm or of harming the baby — this is an emergency, not a mood.
rules.explanation: Postpartum psychosis and severe postnatal depression can present with thoughts of self-harm or of harming the infant, and both carry a real and immediate risk to mother and baby. This is never to be filed as low mood, and never suppressed by any bereavement or sensitivity filter.
rules.requiredAction: Ensure immediate safety of mother and baby, do not leave her alone with the infant unsupervised, and refer for urgent mental-health assessment the same day.

adaptation.whoStatement: Postnatal care includes assessment of maternal emotional wellbeing and referral where a mental-health condition is suspected.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Thoughts of self-harm or of harming the baby are a CRITICAL, non-overridable danger sign requiring same-day assessment.
adaptation.rationale: The general recommendation to 'assess wellbeing and refer' is too soft for the specific, immediately dangerous presentation. Making it CRITICAL and non-overridable stops it being softened away, particularly after a loss, where the risk is higher and the instinct to be gentle is strongest.

rules.name: Mastitis or breast abscess
rules.message: Breast pain, redness or a lump — assess for mastitis or abscess.
rules.explanation: A red, painful, swollen area of breast with fever is mastitis; a fluctuant lump is an abscess needing drainage. Continued breastfeeding or expression from the affected breast is part of the treatment, not a risk.
rules.requiredAction: Assess, support continued effective milk removal, give antibiotics for mastitis, and refer a suspected abscess for drainage.
sourceRefs: WHO PNC — breastfeeding and breast conditions

adaptation.whoStatement: Breast pain and signs of infection postnatally require assessment and management for mastitis or abscess, with continued breastfeeding support.
